=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): alternate (leaves are attached at successive nodes along the stem, alternating sides; no paired leaves or whorls visible)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): clustered (multiple leaves appear grouped near the apex of the shoot, with short internodes)

B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): compound (each leaf unit has multiple leaflets attached to a central rachis)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): odd-pinnate (the leaflets are arranged along a central axis with one terminal leaflet; leaflets appear to be arranged in pairs with a single terminal leaflet)
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): 7 (approximately 7 leaflets visible per leaf; 3 pairs and one terminal leaflet, consistent with odd-pinnate)
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): alternate (leaflets are arranged alternately along the rachis, not in pairs)

C. Leaf Morphology
    7. Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.)): entire (margins are smooth with no teeth or serrations)
    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): lanceolate (leaflets are elongated with a broad base tapering to a pointed tip)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acuminate (apex tapers to a fine point, gradually narrowing)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): cuneate (base is wedge-shaped, tapering to the petiole)
    11. Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (primary vein runs lengthwise with secondary veins branching off perpendicularly)
    12. Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): visible, closely spaced, numerous (secondary veins are clearly visible, running parallel to each other and perpendicular to midrib, forming a fine network)
    13. Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): glabrous, dull (surface appears smooth and non-glossy, no visible hairs or wrinkles)
    14. Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible trichomes or hairs on leaf surface)
    15. Petiole length (short / long): short (petiole is short, supporting the compound leaf structure without elongation)
    16. Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (petiole is round in cross-section, no wings or grooves visible)

D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): herbaceous (stem appears soft and green, typical of young seedling; no bark or woody texture evident)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs on stem)
    19. Stem color: green (stem is uniformly green, consistent with young growth)
    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth (surface appears smooth without ridges or lenticels)

E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21. Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent (no stipules visible at leaf base or node)
    22. Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed (no exudate or latex visible upon inspection)
    23. Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent (no visible pulvinus at leaflet or leaf base; not applicable unless family known, but no evidence)
    24. Tendrils (present / absent): absent (no tendrils present)

F. Notes: Some leaflets show minor damage including small holes and margin irregularities, likely due to physical disturbance or minor feeding; pink tag is present for identification, not part of plant. All images show the same seedling from multiple angles, confirming observations. No clear evidence of flowering or fruiting structures. Leaflet count may vary slightly due to angle and occlusion, but 7 is the most consistent estimate.
